import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Isomorphism problem of Coxeter groups

It is an unresolved problem in group theory to determine whether or not two Coxeter groups
(specified by their Coxeter diagrams, or equivalently by their Coxeter matrices) are isomorphic as
abstract groups. Equivalently, the problem asks to determine, for a given Coxeter group $W$, the
possible subsets $S$ of $W$ that are Coxeter generating sets for $W$ (that is, for which $(W, S)$
is a Coxeter system).

As in the literature (Problem 1 of Mühlherr's survey, the "classic isomorphism problem" of
Santos Rego and Schwer), this is a decision problem about finitely generated Coxeter groups: is
there an algorithm which, given two Coxeter matrices $M$ and $M'$ of finite rank, decides whether
the Coxeter groups $W(M)$ and $W(M')$ are isomorphic? The expected answer is "yes", but the problem
is open.

## Implementation notes

A Coxeter matrix of finite rank is a `CoxeterMatrix (Fin n)` for some `n : ℕ`; every Coxeter
matrix over a finite index type is a reindexing of one of these, and reindexing does not change
the Coxeter group up to isomorphism (`CoxeterMatrix.reindexGroupEquiv`). Mathlib encodes the entry
$\infty$ of a Coxeter matrix as `0`.

Decidability is expressed with Mathlib's `ComputablePred`, which requires a `Primcodable` encoding
of the inputs. We encode a finite-rank Coxeter matrix by its table of entries, a `List (List ℕ)`,
and transport the resulting `Primcodable` instance to the type
`FinCoxeterMatrix := Σ n, CoxeterMatrix (Fin n)` along an explicit bijection.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, *Isomorphism problem of Coxeter groups*](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Isomorphism_problem_of_Coxeter_groups)
- [Wikipedia, *List of unsolved problems in mathematics*](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [B. Mühlherr, *The isomorphism problem for Coxeter groups*](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0506572),
  Problems 1 and 3.
- [Y. Santos Rego, P. Schwer, *The galaxy of Coxeter groups*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2211.17038),
  Section 3.2, "The (classic) isomorphism problem".
-/

/-- The `(i, j)`-entry of a table `L : List (List ℕ)` (with default value `0`). -/
def entry (L : List (List ℕ)) (i j : ℕ) : ℕ := (L.getD i []).getD j 0

blocks.docstring:
A table `L : List (List ℕ)` is a *Coxeter table* if it is square, symmetric, and its
`(i, j)`-entry equals `1` exactly when `i = j`. These are precisely the tables of entries of
finite-rank Coxeter matrices, see `equivTable`.

blocks.name: IsCoxeterTable
blocks.text:
/-- A table `L : List (List ℕ)` is a *Coxeter table* if it is square, symmetric, and its
`(i, j)`-entry equals `1` exactly when `i = j`. These are precisely the tables of entries of
finite-rank Coxeter matrices, see `equivTable`. -/
def IsCoxeterTable (L : List (List ℕ)) : Prop :=
  (∀ row ∈ L, row.length = L.length) ∧
    ∀ i < L.length, ∀ j < L.length, entry L i j = entry L j i ∧ (i = j ↔ entry L i j = 1)

blocks.code:
instance : DecidablePred IsCoxeterTable := fun L => by
  unfold IsCoxeterTable; infer_instance
blocks.text:
instance : DecidablePred IsCoxeterTable := fun L => by
  unfold IsCoxeterTable; infer_instance

theorem primrecRel_forall_lt {β : Type*} [Primcodable β] {R : ℕ → β → Prop}
    (hR : PrimrecRel R) : PrimrecRel fun (n : ℕ) (b : β) => ∀ x < n, R x b :=

@[category API, AMS 3]
theorem primrecPred_isCoxeterTable : PrimrecPred IsCoxeterTable := by
  have h₁ : PrimrecPred fun L : List (List ℕ) => ∀ row ∈ L, row.length = L.length :=
    (PrimrecRel.forall_mem_list (R := fun (row : List ℕ) (L : List (List ℕ)) =>
      row.length = L.length) (Primrec.eq.comp (list_length.comp fst) (list_length.comp snd))).comp
      .id .id
  have e₁ : Primrec fun p : ℕ × (ℕ × List (List ℕ)) => entry p.2.2 p.2.1 p.1 :=
    primrec_entry.comp ((snd.comp snd).pair ((fst.comp snd).pair fst))
  have e₂ : Primrec fun p : ℕ × (ℕ × List (List ℕ)) => entry p.2.2 p.1 p.2.1 :=
    primrec_entry.comp ((snd.comp snd).pair (fst.pair (fst.comp snd)))
  have hij : PrimrecPred fun p : ℕ × (ℕ × List (List ℕ)) => p.2.1 = p.1 :=
    Primrec.eq.comp (fst.comp snd) fst
  have h1 : PrimrecPred fun p : ℕ × (ℕ × List (List ℕ)) => entry p.2.2 p.2.1 p.1 = 1 :=
    Primrec.eq.comp e₁ (const 1)
  have h₀ : PrimrecRel fun (j : ℕ) (q : ℕ × List (List ℕ)) =>
      entry q.2 q.1 j = entry q.2 j q.1 ∧ (q.1 = j ↔ entry q.2 q.1 j = 1) :=
    (Primrec.eq.comp e₁ e₂).and (((hij.and h1).or (hij.not.and h1.not)).of_eq fun _ =>
      iff_iff_and_or_not_and_not.symm)
  have h₂ : PrimrecRel fun (i : ℕ) (L : List (List ℕ)) => ∀ j < L.length,
      entry L i j = entry L j i ∧ (i = j ↔ entry L i j = 1) :=
    (primrecRel_forall_lt h₀).comp (list_length.comp snd) (fst.pair snd)
  exact h₁.and ((primrecRel_forall_lt h₂).comp list_length .id)

  have h₁ : PrimrecPred fun L : List (List ℕ) => ∀ row ∈ L, row.length = L.length :=
    (PrimrecRel.forall_mem_list (R := fun (row : List ℕ) (L : List (List ℕ)) =>
      row.length = L.length) (Primrec.eq.comp (list_length.comp fst) (list_length.comp snd))).comp
      .id .id
  have e₁ : Primrec fun p : ℕ × (ℕ × List (List ℕ)) => entry p.2.2 p.2.1 p.1 :=
    primrec_entry.comp ((snd.comp snd).pair ((fst.comp snd).pair fst))
  have e₂ : Primrec fun p : ℕ × (ℕ × List (List ℕ)) => entry p.2.2 p.1 p.2.1 :=
    primrec_entry.comp ((snd.comp snd).pair (fst.pair (fst.comp snd)))
  have hij : PrimrecPred fun p : ℕ × (ℕ × List (List ℕ)) => p.2.1 = p.1 :=
    Primrec.eq.comp (fst.comp snd) fst
  have h1 : PrimrecPred fun p : ℕ × (ℕ × List (List ℕ)) => entry p.2.2 p.2.1 p.1 = 1 :=
    Primrec.eq.comp e₁ (const 1)

      entry q.2 q.1 j = entry q.2 j q.1 ∧ (q.1 = j ↔ entry q.2 q.1 j = 1) :=
    (Primrec.eq.comp e₁ e₂).and (((hij.and h1).or (hij.not.and h1.not)).of_eq fun _ =>
      iff_iff_and_or_not_and_not.symm)

      entry L i j = entry L j i ∧ (i = j ↔ entry L i j = 1) :=
    (primrecRel_forall_lt h₀).comp (list_length.comp snd) (fst.pair snd)
  exact h₁.and ((primrecRel_forall_lt h₂).comp list_length .id)

blocks.code:
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem isCoxeterTable_toTable {n : ℕ} (M : CoxeterMatrix (Fin n)) :
    IsCoxeterTable (toTable M) := by
  refine ⟨fun row hrow => ?_, fun i hi j hj => ?_⟩
  · obtain ⟨k, rfl⟩ := List.mem_ofFn.mp hrow
    simp [toTable]
  · rw [length_toTable] at hi hj
    rw [entry_toTable M ⟨i, hi⟩ ⟨j, hj⟩, entry_toTable M ⟨j, hj⟩ ⟨i, hi⟩]
    refine ⟨M.symmetric _ _, fun h => ?_, fun h => ?_⟩
    · subst h
      exact M.diagonal _
    · by_contra h'
      exact M.off_diagonal ⟨i, hi⟩ ⟨j, hj⟩ (fun e => h' (congrArg Fin.val e)) h

blocks.code:
def ofTable (L : List (List ℕ)) (hL : IsCoxeterTable L) : CoxeterMatrix (Fin L.length) where
  M := Matrix.of fun i j => entry L i j
  isSymm := Matrix.IsSymm.ext fun i j => (hL.2 j j.2 i i.2).1
  diagonal i := (hL.2 i i.2 i i.2).2.mp rfl
  off_diagonal i j h h' := h (Fin.ext ((hL.2 i i.2 j j.2).2.mpr h'))
blocks.docstring: The Coxeter matrix with a given Coxeter table of entries.

theorem sigma_mk_eq {m n : ℕ} (h : m = n) (X : CoxeterMatrix (Fin m)) (Y : CoxeterMatrix (Fin n))
    (hXY : ∀ i j : Fin m, X i j = Y (Fin.cast h i) (Fin.cast h j)) :
    (⟨m, X⟩ : FinCoxeterMatrix) = ⟨n, Y⟩ := by
  subst h
  congr
  ext i j
  exact hXY i j

def equivTable : FinCoxeterMatrix ≃ {L : List (List ℕ) // IsCoxeterTable L} where
  toFun M := ⟨toTable M.2, isCoxeterTable_toTable M.2⟩
  invFun L := ⟨L.1.length, ofTable L.1 L.2⟩
  left_inv := by
    rintro ⟨n, M⟩
    exact sigma_mk_eq (length_toTable M) _ _ fun i j =>
      entry_toTable M (Fin.cast (length_toTable M) i) (Fin.cast (length_toTable M) j)
  right_inv := by
    rintro ⟨L, hL⟩
    refine Subtype.ext (List.ext_getElem (length_toTable _) fun i h₁ h₂ => ?_)
    have hrow : L.length = L[i].length := (hL.1 _ (List.getElem_mem h₂)).symm
    refine List.ext_getElem (by simpa [toTable] using hrow) fun j h₃ h₄ => ?_
    simp [toTable, ofTable, entry, h₄]

blocks.docstring:
**Isomorphism problem of Coxeter groups.** Is there an algorithm which, given two Coxeter groups
$W(M)$ and $W(M')$ specified by their Coxeter diagrams (equivalently, by finite-rank Coxeter
matrices $M$ and $M'$), decides whether or not $W(M)$ and $W(M')$ are isomorphic as abstract
groups?

Formally: is the predicate "$W(M) \cong W(M')$" on pairs $(M, M')$ of finite-rank Coxeter matrices
computable? The answer is expected to be "yes", but the problem is open.

$W(M)$ and $W(M')$ specified by their Coxeter diagrams (equivalently, by finite-rank Coxeter
matrices $M$ and $M'$), decides whether or not $W(M)$ and $W(M')$ are isomorphic as abstract

claims.decomposer_note: This is Mühlherr's Problem 1 / Santos Rego–Schwer's 'classic isomorphism problem': a decision problem, so the Prop is decidability (e.g. `answer(sorry) ↔ ComputablePred` of the relation `Nonempty (M.Group ≃* M'.Group)` on pairs of Coxeter matrices over finite index types, with a Primcodable encoding); restrict to finite rank (finitely generated) Coxeter groups as all sources do, isomorphism is as abstract groups (not type-preserving), and note Mathlib's `CoxeterMatrix` encodes ∞ as 0; the expected answer in the literature is 'yes' but it is open.
claims.reviewer_why: All eight candidates state the same mathematics (Mühlherr Problem 1 / Santos Rego–Schwer 'classic isomorphism problem'): uniform decidability, via Mathlib's `ComputablePred`, of abstract-group isomorphism `Nonempty (M.Group ≃* M'.Group)` on pairs of finite-rank Coxeter matrices (∞ encoded as 0, rank 0 harmlessly included), with `answer(True)` = an algorithm exists (the expected but open answer). They differ only in encoding. c06 has the most direct statement — the predicate lives on `FinCoxeterMatrix × FinCoxeterMatrix` with `FinCoxeterMatrix := Σ n, CoxeterMatrix (Fin n)` exactly as the decomposition notes suggest — and its `Primcodable` instance is honest and Lean-verified: `Primcodable.ofEquiv` from `Primcodable.subtype` over Mathlib's standard `List (List ℕ)` encoding along an explicit bijection `equivTable` (table of entries), with API lemmas and `decide` tests. It is an unresolved problem in the mathematical field of group theory to determine whether or not two Coxeter groups (specified by their Coxeter diagrams) are isomorphic as abstract groups.  Equivalently, the problem asks to determine, for a given Coxeter group $W$, the possible subsets $S$ of $W$ that are Coxeter generating sets for $W$ (that is, for which $(W,S)$ is a Coxeter system).
A slight generalization of the problem can be made by asking to find to all isomorphisms from one group onto the other.
In 2022, Yuri Santos Rego and Petra Schwer introduced a new framework to deal with the problem (a finite dimensional, locally finite, ranked simplicial complex to capture isomorphisms between finite rank Coxeter systems) and asked more 
related open questions motivated by it.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Isomorphism problem of Coxeter groups

It is an unresolved problem in group theory to determine whether or not two Coxeter groups
(specified by their Coxeter diagrams, or equivalently by their Coxeter matrices) are isomorphic as
abstract groups. Equivalently, the problem asks to determine, for a given Coxeter group $W$, the
possible subsets $S$ of $W$ that are Coxeter generating sets for $W$ (that is, for which $(W, S)$
is a Coxeter system).

As in the literature (Problem 1 of Mühlherr's survey, the "classic isomorphism problem" of
Santos Rego and Schwer), this is a decision problem about finitely generated Coxeter groups: is
there an algorithm which, given two Coxeter matrices $M$ and $M'$ of finite rank, decides whether
the Coxeter groups $W(M)$ and $W(M')$ are isomorphic? The expected answer is "yes", but the problem
is open.

## Implementation notes

A Coxeter matrix of finite rank is a `CoxeterMatrix (Fin n)` for some `n : ℕ`; every Coxeter
matrix over a finite index type is a reindexing of one of these, and reindexing does not change
the Coxeter group up to isomorphism (`CoxeterMatrix.reindexGroupEquiv`). Mathlib encodes the entry
$\infty$ of a Coxeter matrix as `0`.

Decidability is expressed with Mathlib's `ComputablePred`, which requires a `Primcodable` encoding
of the inputs. We encode a finite-rank Coxeter matrix by its table of entries, a `List (List ℕ)`,
and transport the resulting `Primcodable` instance to the type
`FinCoxeterMatrix := Σ n, CoxeterMatrix (Fin n)` along an explicit bijection.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, *Isomorphism problem of Coxeter groups*](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Isomorphism_problem_of_Coxeter_groups)
- [Wikipedia, *List of unsolved problems in mathematics*](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [B. Mühlherr, *The isomorphism problem for Coxeter groups*](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0506572),
  Problems 1 and 3.
- [Y. Santos Rego, P. Schwer, *The galaxy of Coxeter groups*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2211.17038),
  Section 3.2, "The (classic) isomorphism problem".
-/

namespace IsomorphismProblemOfCoxeterGroups

open Primrec

/-- A Coxeter matrix of finite rank, indexed by `Fin n` for some `n : ℕ`. -/
abbrev FinCoxeterMatrix := Σ n : ℕ, CoxeterMatrix (Fin n)

section Encoding

/-- The `(i, j)`-entry of a table `L : List (List ℕ)` (with default value `0`). -/
def entry (L : List (List ℕ)) (i j : ℕ) : ℕ := (L.getD i []).getD j 0

/-- A table `L : List (List ℕ)` is a *Coxeter table* if it is square, symmetric, and its
`(i, j)`-entry equals `1` exactly when `i = j`. These are precisely the tables of entries of
finite-rank Coxeter matrices, see `equivTable`. -/
def IsCoxeterTable (L : List (List ℕ)) : Prop :=
  (∀ row ∈ L, row.length = L.length) ∧
    ∀ i < L.length, ∀ j < L.length, entry L i j = entry L j i ∧ (i = j ↔ entry L i j = 1)

instance : DecidablePred IsCoxeterTable := fun L => by
  unfold IsCoxeterTable; infer_instance

@[category API, AMS 3]
theorem primrec_entry :
    Primrec fun p : List (List ℕ) × (ℕ × ℕ) => entry p.1 p.2.1 p.2.2 :=
  (list_getD 0).comp ((list_getD ([] : List ℕ)).comp fst (fst.comp snd)) (snd.comp snd)

/-- Bounded universal quantification over `ℕ` preserves primitive recursive relations. This
generalises `PrimrecRel.forall_lt` from relations on `ℕ × ℕ` to relations on `ℕ × β`. -/
@[category API, AMS 3]
theorem primrecRel_forall_lt {β : Type*} [Primcodable β] {R : ℕ → β → Prop}
    (hR : PrimrecRel R) : PrimrecRel fun (n : ℕ) (b : β) => ∀ x < n, R x b :=
  PrimrecPred.of_eq ((PrimrecRel.forall_mem_list hR).comp (list_range.comp fst) snd) fun _ => by
    simp

/-- Being a Coxeter table is primitive recursive, so that Coxeter tables form a `Primcodable`
type. -/
@[category API, AMS 3]
theorem primrecPred_isCoxeterTable : PrimrecPred IsCoxeterTable := by
  have h₁ : PrimrecPred fun L : List (List ℕ) => ∀ row ∈ L, row.length = L.length :=
    (PrimrecRel.forall_mem_list (R := fun (row : List ℕ) (L : List (List ℕ)) =>
      row.length = L.length) (Primrec.eq.comp (list_length.comp fst) (list_length.comp snd))).comp
      .id .id
  have e₁ : Primrec fun p : ℕ × (ℕ × List (List ℕ)) => entry p.2.2 p.2.1 p.1 :=
    primrec_entry.comp ((snd.comp snd).pair ((fst.comp snd).pair fst))
  have e₂ : Primrec fun p : ℕ × (ℕ × List (List ℕ)) => entry p.2.2 p.1 p.2.1 :=
    primrec_entry.comp ((snd.comp snd).pair (fst.pair (fst.comp snd)))
  have hij : PrimrecPred fun p : ℕ × (ℕ × List (List ℕ)) => p.2.1 = p.1 :=
    Primrec.eq.comp (fst.comp snd) fst
  have h1 : PrimrecPred fun p : ℕ × (ℕ × List (List ℕ)) => entry p.2.2 p.2.1 p.1 = 1 :=
    Primrec.eq.comp e₁ (const 1)
  have h₀ : PrimrecRel fun (j : ℕ) (q : ℕ × List (List ℕ)) =>
      entry q.2 q.1 j = entry q.2 j q.1 ∧ (q.1 = j ↔ entry q.2 q.1 j = 1) :=
    (Primrec.eq.comp e₁ e₂).and (((hij.and h1).or (hij.not.and h1.not)).of_eq fun _ =>
      iff_iff_and_or_not_and_not.symm)
  have h₂ : PrimrecRel fun (i : ℕ) (L : List (List ℕ)) => ∀ j < L.length,
      entry L i j = entry L j i ∧ (i = j ↔ entry L i j = 1) :=
    (primrecRel_forall_lt h₀).comp (list_length.comp snd) (fst.pair snd)
  exact h₁.and ((primrecRel_forall_lt h₂).comp list_length .id)

/-- The table of entries of a finite-rank Coxeter matrix, as a list of rows. -/
def toTable {n : ℕ} (M : CoxeterMatrix (Fin n)) : List (List ℕ) :=
  List.ofFn fun i => List.ofFn fun j => M i j

@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem length_toTable {n : ℕ} (M : CoxeterMatrix (Fin n)) : (toTable M).length = n :=
  List.length_ofFn

@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem entry_toTable {n : ℕ} (M : CoxeterMatrix (Fin n)) (i j : Fin n) :
    entry (toTable M) i j = M i j := by
  simp [entry, toTable, i.2, j.2]

@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem isCoxeterTable_toTable {n : ℕ} (M : CoxeterMatrix (Fin n)) :
    IsCoxeterTable (toTable M) := by
  refine ⟨fun row hrow => ?_, fun i hi j hj => ?_⟩
  · obtain ⟨k, rfl⟩ := List.mem_ofFn.mp hrow
    simp [toTable]
  · rw [length_toTable] at hi hj
    rw [entry_toTable M ⟨i, hi⟩ ⟨j, hj⟩, entry_toTable M ⟨j, hj⟩ ⟨i, hi⟩]
    refine ⟨M.symmetric _ _, fun h => ?_, fun h => ?_⟩
    · subst h
      exact M.diagonal _
    · by_contra h'
      exact M.off_diagonal ⟨i, hi⟩ ⟨j, hj⟩ (fun e => h' (congrArg Fin.val e)) h

/-- The Coxeter matrix with a given Coxeter table of entries. -/
def ofTable (L : List (List ℕ)) (hL : IsCoxeterTable L) : CoxeterMatrix (Fin L.length) where
  M := Matrix.of fun i j => entry L i j
  isSymm := Matrix.IsSymm.ext fun i j => (hL.2 j j.2 i i.2).1
  diagonal i := (hL.2 i i.2 i i.2).2.mp rfl
  off_diagonal i j h h' := h (Fin.ext ((hL.2 i i.2 j j.2).2.mpr h'))

@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem sigma_mk_eq {m n : ℕ} (h : m = n) (X : CoxeterMatrix (Fin m)) (Y : CoxeterMatrix (Fin n))
    (hXY : ∀ i j : Fin m, X i j = Y (Fin.cast h i) (Fin.cast h j)) :
    (⟨m, X⟩ : FinCoxeterMatrix) = ⟨n, Y⟩ := by
  subst h
  congr
  ext i j
  exact hXY i j

/-- Finite-rank Coxeter matrices correspond bijectively to Coxeter tables. -/
def equivTable : FinCoxeterMatrix ≃ {L : List (List ℕ) // IsCoxeterTable L} where
  toFun M := ⟨toTable M.2, isCoxeterTable_toTable M.2⟩
  invFun L := ⟨L.1.length, ofTable L.1 L.2⟩
  left_inv := by
    rintro ⟨n, M⟩
    exact sigma_mk_eq (length_toTable M) _ _ fun i j =>
      entry_toTable M (Fin.cast (length_toTable M) i) (Fin.cast (length_toTable M) j)
  right_inv := by
    rintro ⟨L, hL⟩
    refine Subtype.ext (List.ext_getElem (length_toTable _) fun i h₁ h₂ => ?_)
    have hrow : L.length = L[i].length := (hL.1 _ (List.getElem_mem h₂)).symm
    refine List.ext_getElem (by simpa [toTable] using hrow) fun j h₃ h₄ => ?_
    simp [toTable, ofTable, entry, h₄]

/-- Finite-rank Coxeter matrices form a `Primcodable` type: a Coxeter matrix is encoded by its
table of entries. -/
instance : Primcodable FinCoxeterMatrix :=
  @Primcodable.ofEquiv _ _ (Primcodable.subtype primrecPred_isCoxeterTable) equivTable

@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem toTable_A₃ : toTable (CoxeterMatrix.Aₙ 3) = [[1, 3, 2], [3, 1, 3], [2, 3, 1]] := by
  decide

@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isCoxeterTable_example : IsCoxeterTable [[1, 3, 0], [3, 1, 4], [0, 4, 1]] := by
  decide

@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem not_isCoxeterTable_example : ¬ IsCoxeterTable [[1, 2], [3, 1]] := by
  decide

@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem equivTable_A₃ :
    equivTable ⟨3, CoxeterMatrix.Aₙ 3⟩ = ⟨[[1, 3, 2], [3, 1, 3], [2, 3, 1]], by decide⟩ :=
  Subtype.ext toTable_A₃

@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem equivTable_symm_fst :
    (equivTable.symm ⟨[[1, 3, 0], [3, 1, 4], [0, 4, 1]], by decide⟩).1 = 3 :=
  rfl

end Encoding

-/
@[category research open, AMS 3 20]
theorem isomorphism_problem_of_coxeter_groups.variants.coxeter_generating_sets :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ComputablePred fun p : FinCoxeterMatrix × FinCoxeterMatrix =>
      ∃ S : Set p.1.2.Group, IsCoxeterGeneratingSet p.2.2 S := by
  sorry

end IsomorphismProblemOfCoxeterGroups

items: Decision problem: 'determine whether two Coxeter groups are isomorphic' is read (as in Mühlherr Problem 1 and Santos Rego–Schwer's 'classic isomorphism problem') as the existence of an algorithm deciding isomorphism, formalized with Mathlib's `ComputablePred`; `answer(True)` means the problem is decidable (the expected answer).

Finite rank: inputs are `FinCoxeterMatrix := Σ n : ℕ, CoxeterMatrix (Fin n)`, following all sources, which treat finitely generated Coxeter groups. Every Coxeter matrix over a finite index type is a reindexing of one over `Fin n`, and reindexing preserves the group up to isomorphism (`CoxeterMatrix.reindexGroupEquiv`), so nothing is lost.

Coxeter diagram vs. Coxeter matrix: the input is taken to be the Coxeter matrix (equivalent data to the Coxeter diagram); Mathlib encodes the entry ∞ as 0, so all Coxeter groups (including those with infinite entries) are covered.
Isomorphism 'as abstract groups' is `Nonempty (M.Group ≃* M'.Group)` (the repository idiom), not a type-preserving isomorphism.

Encoding for `ComputablePred`: Mathlib lacks `Primcodable` for Sigma types, so `Primcodable FinCoxeterMatrix` is built via `Primcodable.ofEquiv` from an explicit bijection `equivTable` with the subtype `{L : List (List ℕ) // IsCoxeterTable L}`, whose predicate is proved `PrimrecPred`. This is the natural encoding (table of entries), so the notion of computability is the standard one; I deliberately avoided the `Primcodable.ofDenumerable` shortcut, which could change the computability notion. Reviewers should check `IsCoxeterTable`, `equivTable`, and `primrecPred_isCoxeterTable`.

The Primcodable instance and the encoding helpers live in the problem file (the task allowed a single file); in a real PR they might better be placed in FormalConjecturesForMathlib. `primrecRel_forall_lt` generalises Mathlib's `PrimrecRel.forall_lt` (which is restricted to relations on ℕ × ℕ) to relations ℕ → β → Prop.

Variant slot: the literal 'determine all Coxeter generating sets S ⊆ W' is not a finite decision problem (the set of such S is infinite), so, following the decomposition notes, it is modeled as deciding, for given (M, M'), whether W(M) admits a Coxeter generating set S with (W(M), S) a Coxeter system of type M'. The type of S is recorded via Mathlib's `CoxeterSystem M' W` with `S = Set.range cs.simple`. The API lemma `exists_isCoxeterGeneratingSet_iff` shows this predicate is equivalent to `Nonempty (W ≃* M'.Group)`, so the two slots are trivially equivalent, as the article's 'Equivalently' asserts.
The rank-0 (empty) Coxeter matrix is included as an input; it presents no degenerate issue (its group is trivial).
AMS tags: main statements tagged 20 (group theory; decision problems in groups are 20F10); primitive-recursion helper lemmas tagged 3 (logic/computability).
